name: @olai/web
//exports: None. This package has two products and neither is an import: a SCRIPT (`bun packages/web/src/build.ts <dist>`, run by default.nix and by `just build-client`) and the directory it writes. The one thing here that IS imported across a package boundary is src/client/testids.ts, and it is imported by path from packages/tests — a declared export list would suggest a library this is not.
//dependencies: @olai/surface for the wire, @olai/format for everything derived — the client computes nothing about the format on its own. @olai/fonts is the typefaces, on the entry a PAGE reads: the client draws the picker off that table. Its `./build` subpath is the other reader and the one this package's own build imports — the generated `@font-face` sheet plus the woff2 files it names, which src/build.ts appends and copies. Neither half is authored here: the package that owns the faces owns the words for them and the derivation that converts them. The remark/rehype set renders notes, documents, titles (inline-only) and the agent's replies at view time, through ONE pipeline: remark-gfm for footnotes, rehype-sanitize for what may reach innerHTML, rehype-autolink-headings for the link a heading needs before a document can be surveyed or jumped around (src/client/markdown/anchors.ts, which also says what single value the sanitiser's allowlist had to admit for them). The ID a heading is linked BY is not a dependency any more: it is @olai/format's rule (src/client/markdown/slugs.ts is the plugin that spends it), because the same slug has to be what a document's face promises and what the page lands at, and rehype-slug was a second answer to that, and rehype-highlight for fenced code — SHIPPED BY THIS SERVER rather than fetched from a CDN, which is the whole reason it is a dependency here instead of a script tag. It rides in a chunk of its own (src/client/markdown/pipeline.ts, split out by the `import()` in src/client/markdown/chunk.ts) so an outline's first paint does not carry it; same origin, same immutable /assets/ pin, still nothing asked of anyone else. `lowlight` and `highlight.js` are rehype-highlight's own dependencies, declared here because src/client/markdown/pipeline.ts imports them DIRECTLY: the `languages` option replaces the default set rather than extending it, so naming Nix means naming `lowlight`'s `common` beside it and taking the grammar off `highlight.js`. Under the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) a transitive dependency is nested where nothing outside it can see, so an undeclared one is a build that fails to resolve. @types/hast types the one tree this package walks itself (src/client/markdown/rewrite.ts, inline.ts). @solid-primitives/scheduled throttles the re-render of an answer that is still arriving (src/client/chat/Entry.tsx). @kobalte/core is the SolidJS ecosystem's accessible primitives, and it is here for the row's ••• menu (src/client/menu/NodeMenu.tsx uses its DropdownMenu, which owns being open, the placement, the two dismissals and the arrow keys) and for src/client/dismiss.ts, which reaches the same library one layer down (createInteractOutside / createEscapeKeyDown) so the panels this client still draws itself shut by the code the one primitive shuts by. HACKING.md's SolidJS rule is the standing argument for both. The babel presets exist only for the Bun build's Solid JSX transform (src/build.ts explains why Bun's own transform cannot be used).
//tailwind: TWO entries, and the second is not redundant. @tailwindcss/cli is the binary src/build.ts spawns. `tailwindcss` is what `@import "tailwindcss"` inside src/client/styles.css resolves — and under the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) a transitive dependency of the CLI is nested where nothing outside it can see, so the CLI fails with "Can't resolve 'tailwindcss'" until this package declares it directly. Hoisted trees (srid/drishti) never notice; this one does.
